name: pulse_mechanical_ventilation
description: A patient on a pressure-control mechanical ventilator in the real Pulse engine: the respiratory circuit combined with the ventilator circuit, emitting breathing mechanics, lung compartments and the ventilator's monitor values. Defaults follow Pulse's HowTo_VentilationMechanics (intubated; PC-AC 19/5 cmH2O, 12 bpm).

model_type.description: ventilation_mechanics = the airway circuit alone (no blood, no chemoreflex); whole_body = coupled to the rest of the body

patient_file.description: Patient in <install>/bin/patients (on whole_body, also a path). ventilation_mechanics starts from it; on whole_body it replaces state_file, stabilized once (about 13 s) and then cached

circuit_modifiers.description: Circuit path or node name -> multiplier on the resistance, compliance or volume Pulse initializes it with (whole_body only). The patient is stabilized with them (about 25 s the first time, then cached), so the rest of the body adapts: a different patient, not a perturbation

state_file.description: Stabilized Pulse patient state in <install>/bin/states (whole_body only; set this or patient_file, not both)

interval.description: Seconds per update; 0.02 (Pulse's timestep) resolves per-beat/per-breath waveforms. A non-binary-exact interval can lose the final update of a run to float time accumulation.

point_reads.description: Also read every node and path of the circuit drawing (whole_body only), under circuits/<circuit>_points/

left_compliance_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory left compliance multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

right_compliance_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory right compliance multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

left_inspiratory_resistance_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory left inspiratory resistance multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

left_expiratory_resistance_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory left expiratory resistance multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

right_inspiratory_resistance_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory right inspiratory resistance multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

right_expiratory_resistance_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory right expiratory resistance multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

upper_inspiratory_resistance_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory upper inspiratory resistance multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

upper_expiratory_resistance_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory upper expiratory resistance multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

respiration_rate_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory respiration rate multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

tidal_volume_multiplier.description: Pulse respiratory tidal volume multiplier (1.0 = unmodified)

pulse.doc:
Bridge to one real Pulse engine, exposing the selected circuit modules.

``config.modules`` names entries of ``viva_pulse.circuits.MODULES``. Each
module contributes a port subtree named after it:

- outputs: the module's Pulse data requests as ``float`` ports, at the
  module's nested paths (e.g. ``cardiovascular/central/aorta/pressure_mmHg``);
- inputs, under the single ``setpoints`` port: the module's setpoints as
  ``overwrite[float]`` ports whose schema default is the baseline value,
  forwarded to Pulse as actions only on change (e.g.
  ``setpoints/cardiovascular/hemorrhage_severity``).

Inputs and outputs use disjoint top-level port names on purpose:
process-bigraph projects ``initial_state()`` through the input wires as
well as the output wires, so a shared name would copy readings into the
setpoint store.

Outputs follow ``PulseProcess``'s contract. ``initial_state()`` seeds each
store with the loaded state's reading and every update emits
``current - previous``, so the store always equals Pulse's own value.
``irreversible_state`` turns True once Pulse reports an irreversible state;
the engine is not advanced after that. Identical requests from different
modules share one Pulse request. A request that Pulse cannot serve (it
returns NaN) raises at load or at the update where it appears, naming the
request. A module's ``check_loaded`` sees its readings at load and can reject
a state that contradicts its setpoint baselines. All changed setpoint groups
are validated before any action is sent, as is the airway rule: at most one
module's ``airway_device`` connected, and none connecting in the update in
which another disconnects.

WholeBody loads a stabilized ``state_file``, or, when ``patient_file`` is
set instead, that patient's state, stabilized once and then cached (see
``viva_pulse.patients``); setting both raises. ``circuit_modifiers`` (circuit
path or node name -> multiplier) stabilizes the patient with Pulse's
configuration Modifiers, also cached; whole_body only. VentilationMechanics has no
state files, so it initializes from ``patient_file`` and then settles (see
``_settle``) before t = 0; setting ``state_file`` on it raises, instead of
being silently ignored.
Setpoints, including connecting a ventilator, apply from the first update,
so row 0 always shows the engine as loaded or settled.

A module with ``prepare_state`` (the ``*_points`` modules) makes construction
read and edit ``state_file``, so such a process needs the Pulse install when it
is built, not only at its first update.

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
